title: Microbench standup runbook — week of 2026-06-22
body:
Quick context / purpose:
- Mid-week capture for the microbench experiments and onboarding checklist. This is intentionally terse; use as a living log for tactical handoffs.
- Focus areas this sprint: 4-bit quantization fidelity (INT4/FP4 variants), KV-cache interaction with prefix caching, and regression triage on the eval harness.

Summary snapshot (top-line):
- Microbench run 2026-06-22 10:00: baseline vs int4-fast vs fp4-sparse on rtx-a100-32GB.
  - baseline FP16 p50: 12ms / p95: 28ms (seq=128, batch=1).
  - int4-fast p50: 9.6ms / p95: 26ms, ~20% p50 win, slight p95 tail increase on long histories.
  - fp4-sparse p50: 10.1ms / p95: 24ms — good median, better tail vs int4 in some runs.
- Token-level perplexity delta on eval-set-small: int4-fast +0.8% median, fp4-sparse +0.3%.
- Observed a KV-cache sticky miss pattern when switching between cache-hot and cache-cold sequences (see notes).

What we ran (experiments and quick results):
1) Microbench-A: sequential generation with rolling KV cache warmup
   - Config: seq_len_range [64, 256], batch=1, warmup_prefix=128 tokens.
   - Findings: int4-fast exhibits faster ramp but higher variance when warmup_prefix < model_context/4. Potential root cause: kernel alignment mismatch for packed bits at small prefix sizes.
2) Microbench-B: eval harness replay (10k prompts) comparing sample-based metrics
   - Config: deterministic sampling (greedy) to isolate quant noise.
   - Findings: overall CTR-like quality metrics stable; 1.2% prompts flagged by eval rules as degraded under int4-fast (mostly factuality edgecases).
3) KV-cache fuzz test
   - Repro: alternating hot/cold request sequences across the same worker process (no restart).
   - Symptom: first few tokens after hot->cold switch return slightly truncated continuations (loss of leading token attention).
   - Hypothesis: cache indexing offset not reset on sequence boundary in recent KV-cache rewrite (PR 213).

Notes from the standup (raw, unordered):
- Ravi: chased int4 kernel arithmetic vs FP16 reference on small matrices — saw rounding path that explains a 0.2–0.6% shift on attention logits for 50–60 token context windows. Next action: add unit test that exercises this rounding at 16x16 tile boundary. Ticket ML-4821 assigned.
- Lina: started onboarding checklist for community model (guanaco-13b-ish) — tokenization edgecases noted (emoji + ZWJ sequences) cause length blowup that impacts microbatcher. Added pre-tokenization clamp as temporary mitigation.
- Ethan: triaging eval harness alerts — created a filter for hallucination-rule-7 to reduce noise. Found 120 false positives in last week's run (source: punctuation heuristics).
- Jonas: validated PR 213 on a dedicated node; reproduced KV-cache sticky miss locally. Added logs and suggested reset point after sequence boundary.

Hypotheses and short experiments to prioritize (this sprint):
- H1: Small-prefix int4 variance is caused by bitpacking alignment when prefix length % pack_size != 0. Quick test: pad prefixes to pack_size and re-run microbench A. Expected: variance drop. Owner: Ravi, due 2026-06-24.
- H2: KV-cache sticky miss due to pointer not being cleared on user-level sequence end. Quick patch to zero offset after each sequence and run fuzz harness. Owner: Jonas, due 2026-06-23.
- H3: fp4-sparse better tail because of dynamic exponent preservation for high-variance activations. Need to instrument activation histograms during generation. Owner: Maya, due 2026-06-25.

Action items (explicit, who/when):
- Add alignment unit test for int4 kernels (Ravi) — JIRA ML-4821 — target: 2026-06-24.
- Patch KV-cache reset and smoke test (Jonas) — PR draft by 2026-06-23; link: github PR placeholder (see linked_artifacts).
- Add eval rule whitelist for punctuation heuristics (Ethan) — small patch to eval harness — 2026-06-24.
- Update community model onboarding checklist with tokenization clamp and example failure cases (Lina) — update doc and example scripts — 2026-06-26.
- Run full 50k prompt micro-eval with int4-fast and fp4-sparse on dedicated runner and upload results (Maya + infra) — start 2026-06-25.

Open questions / blockers:
- Is the KV-cache rewrite safe for Dedicated (reserved) multi-tenant nodes? Need SRE signoff for restart policy if we force zero-offset on every sequence boundary. Blocker: SRE availability this week. Contact: sree@redwood.internal.
- Do we accept ~1% median quality delta for int4-fast in exchange for 20% perf win? Need product input from PM. Action: schedule 15m sync with PM Jamie.
- Onboarding checklist: should we automatically clamp tokenized length or surface as opt-in flag? Product decision needed.

Notes to self / friction points observed:
- Microbench runner config files are brittle: switching between seq/batch combos requires manual edits in two places. Create a single canonical runner config and generator wrapper. (TODO).
- Logging verbosity: need lightweight binary logs for microbench to avoid spamming S3 with raw traces. Consider summarized protobuf line format.

Quick logs and snippets (to copy-paste):
- Repro command (local): 
  ./tools/microbench/run.sh --model=community/guanaco-13b --quant=int4-fast --seq=128 --batch=1 --warmup=128 --out=results/int4-fast-2026-06-22.json
- Fuzz harness: 
  python infra/kv_fuzz.py --cycles=20000 --seed=20260622 --log=kv-fuzz-2206.log

Next syncs / schedule:
- Daily 10:30 standup (15m) this week to close actions; 3x week deep-dive on Mon/Wed/Fri at 14:00.
- Tentative PM sync Thu 2026-06-24 09:00 to discuss int4 tradeoffs.

Appendix (raw metrics links and attachments):
- short-run metrics CSV uploaded to /prod-research/microbench/2026-06-22/int4-fast-summary.csv (infra will move to long-term storage later).
- Screenshots attached in Drive (linked in Confluence page).

Random brainstorm (parking lot):
- Could we do a hybrid scheme where prefix tokens use higher precision and tail uses int4 to capture warmup fidelity? Might require per-layer or per-position quant flags — heavy lift but maybe worth prototyping.
- Consider a small synthetic dataset of tokenized edgecases (emoji-heavy, code snippets, math expressions) to stress test tokenization + microbatch combos.

If you read one thing: the KV-cache sticky miss is highest priority for stability. Patch + smoke and then run 50k prompt eval.

Raw edit history: started by Maya 2026-06-22 09:47; updates by Jonas and Ravi 2026-06-23; final notes and action assignment 2026-06-24 11:05.
